description: Acute onset of high fever accompanied by rigors, severe headache, and malaise indicates systemic acute febrile illness.

source: NHS Health A to Z - Common Cold
description: Upper respiratory syndrome coupled with continuous sneezing and rhinorrhea supports acute viral nasopharyngitis (common cold).
Sneezing with mild chills, progressive fatigue, and cough aligns with self-limiting viral coryza.
Upper respiratory signs paired with sudden high pyrexia, rigors, and myalgia strongly support seasonal influenza.
Lower respiratory tract symptoms with purulent phlegm and tachycardia support parenchymal pulmonary consolidation (pneumonia).
Persistent cough, high temperature, dyspnea, and pleuritic chest pain provide strong rule evidence for pneumonia.
Reversible airway symptoms: paroxysmal dyspnea, tight chest discomfort, and mucoid sputum indicate bronchial asthma.
Chronic productive cough with constitutional wasting, fever, and hemoptysis forms cardinal criteria for pulmonary tuberculosis.
Paroxysms of shivering chills followed by high pyrexia and drenching diaphoresis strongly support Plasmodium infection.
Classic periodic febrile triad: rigors, diaphoresis, and headache with emesis matches acute malaria.
